messages:
aisha: ran the eval-harness concurrency sweep on the new small-int8 runner earlier. p50 looks fine but p95 jumps massively when concurrency goes from 8 -> 9. cost/token goes down (weird) but latency SLO violation spikes.

michael: hmm. do you have the heatmap for request timing + kvcache hit rate? could be skewed batching or a KV prefetch order bug.

 aisha: attaching short snippet of the failing test output:```
./perf_runner --model small-int8 --concurrency 9 --qps 200 --duration 60 
[2026-11-12 14:12:03] samples=12000 tokens=1.8M p95=342ms p50=18ms kvcache_hit=0.41
[2026-11-12 14:12:33] samples=12000 tokens=1.8M p95=1200ms p50=20ms kvcache_hit=0.11
```

 aisha: the hanger is that kvcache_hit drops right when p95 spikes. looks like a bad reuse of cache between concurrent requests?

michael: can you dump thread ordering for the runner for that window (print request ids + batch_id)? maybe we are reusing the same KV buffer across workers. also check batch_windowing config.

ci-bot: perf-sweep job #4821 reported flakiness: 1 failed run out of 47 for test `perf_runner/concurrency_sweep_small_int8` (see artifacts).

 s ophia: (taking notes) this smells like a race in the runner's prefetch path. I remember a recent change to prefetch scheduling where we moved to round-robin across executors — could have introduced shared state.

 jordan: quick idea: add a per-request prefetch token and assert distinct buffer pointer in debug build. low-cost assert to push into CI.

 aisha: good call. i'll add an assert in debug that verifies `prefetch_buffer_id != 0 && !seen_before` and re-run. if it trips, we'll get exact request ids.

 michael: also check the eval harness sampler. we recently changed the sample pool to bias recent prompts; if the sampler clusters similar prompt lengths, that can skew batch composition and KV cache locality, making p95 worse at some concurrencies.

 aisha: noted — will run two runs: (1) original sampler (random) (2) new recency-biased sampler and compare heatmaps.

 s ophia: if we confirm it's a sampler interaction, we should add a test that runs both samplers in nightly CI and diffs p95 < 1.2x.

 aisha: local debug run with the debug-assert enabled:```
[DBG] request=rx-17 buffer_id=0x7f9a3c prefetch_seen=false
[DBG] request=rx-18 buffer_id=0x7f9a3c prefetch_seen=true <-- assert triggered
Assertion failed: prefetch_seen == false at runner/prefetch.cc:142
```

 aisha: okay that reproduces it reliably at concurrency 9. looks like two requests are getting the same buffer pointer.

 michael: nailed it. likely a pool acquire race. i'll open a small PR that swaps the pool to use an atomic freelist and add a unit test to simulate N concurrent acquires.

 ci-bot: created PR #2145 by michael: "runner: make prefetch buffer pool thread-safe (atomic freelist)" — perf unit + integration tests added.

 jordan: once PR lands, let's schedule a canary sweep across the dedicated pool for small-int8 (low QPS) and compare cost/token + p95 heatmaps. I'll wire the canary to post results to the perf dashboard.

 s ophia: also add a golden sample set to the eval harness (50 fixed prompts) so we have deterministic regressions for quality & perf across quantization runs. should help catch sampling-induced flakiness.

 aisha: thanks everyone — will re-run the sweeps with PR applied and post artifacts. cc @michael if you want me to run extra debug traces after the PR. :thumbsup:

 ci-bot: perf-sweep artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/artifacts/2026-11-12/1834567890. logs + heatmaps + trace.zip

 aisha: results after PR merged: concurrency 9 p95 back to ~28ms stable, kvcache_hit maintained ~0.43 across window. cost/token same as before. marking this as root-cause: prefetch buffer pool race. will open a follow-up to harden sampler cluster behavior.

 michael: thanks — great catch. let's add a short blurb to the runbook under "eval-harness" about sampler determinism and a checklist for concurrency sweeps.

 sophia: i'll create the runbook note and schedule the golden set to land in nightly CI.

 jordan: can we add an alert on the perf dashboard for p95 jumps > 3x baseline during sweeps? would help us catch this class of regressions early.

 aisha: added that to the TODO list. closing thread once artifacts baked into dashboard. :white_check_mark:
